assignments.name: major_task
assignments.value: Install nginx on the ubuntu 24.04 host

parameters.command: =mkdir -p "{{ $('Create Run ID').first().json.run_dir }}/tasks" "{{ $('Create Run ID').first().json.run_dir }}/reviews" "{{ $('Create Run ID').first().json.workspace }}/memory" && if [ ! -f "{{ $('Create Run ID').first().json.workspace }}/memory/verifier-memory.json" ]; then printf '{"reviews":[]}' > "{{ $('Create Run ID').first().json.workspace }}/memory/verifier-memory.json"; fi

parameters.body:
={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $('Create Run ID').first().json.task_breaker_model, temperature: 0.1, max_tokens: 2000, think: false, response_format: { type: 'json_object' }, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: `You are a Task Breaker. Convert one major task into the minimum useful number of well-defined subtasks. Return ONLY one valid JSON object. No markdown, comments, or text outside the JSON.

Required structure:
{
  "plan_summary":"string",
  "assumptions":["string"],
  "tasks":[{
    "id":"T01",
    "title":"string",
    "objective":"string",
    "rationale":"string",
    "inputs_required":["string"],
    "expected_output":"string",
    "success_criteria":["string"],
    "dependencies":[],
    "risk_level":"low"
  }]
}

Rules:
- Typical 8-10 tasks.
- Hard maximum ${$('Create Run ID').first().json.max_subtasks} tasks.
- Keep all fields concise.
- Each string should normally be one sentence.
- Maximum 3 inputs_required entries.
- Maximum 3 success_criteria entries.
- Planning only. Do not execute commands.
- Each task must be detailed enough for a later coding/tool agent.
- Explain why each task exists.
- Do not invent facts about the target system.
- Unknown required facts should create discovery/precondition tasks.
- Dependencies may reference only earlier task IDs.
- Avoid overlap and duplicate work.
- Success criteria must be measurable.
- risk_level must be low, medium, or high.
- Finish the complete JSON object before stopping.` }, { role: 'user', content: `Major task:
${$('Create Run ID').first().json.major_task}` } ] }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $('Create Run ID').first().json.verifier_model, temperature: 0.1, max_tokens: 300, think:false, response_format: { type: 'json_object' }, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: `You are a strict planning verifier.

Your job is to review exactly ONE proposed subtask against the overall major task.

Evaluate:
- relevance to the major task
- specificity
- whether a later tool/coding agent could execute it
- missing required inputs
- measurable success criteria
- dependency correctness
- overlap or duplication
- unsafe assumptions
- scope

Prior verifier memory may be provided. Use it only to avoid repeating previously identified planning mistakes. Do not fail a task merely because a similar issue appeared previously.

Return ONLY one valid JSON object in this format:
{
  "task_id":"T01",
  "verdict":"PASS",
  "score":8,
  "problems":[],
  "required_changes":[],
  "reason":"5 words"
}

Rules:
- verdict must be PASS or FAIL.
- score must be an integer from 0 to 10.
- PASS requires score >= 8.
- PASS requires no material problems.
- FAIL if required information is materially missing.
- Do not execute anything.
- Do not generate shell commands.
- Do not use markdown.
- Do not include text outside the JSON object.` }, { role: 'user', content: `MAJOR TASK:

${$json.major_task}

TASK TO REVIEW:

${JSON.stringify($json.task, null, 2)}

PRIOR VERIFIER MEMORY:

${JSON.stringify($json.verifier_memory, null, 2)}` } ] }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({   model: $("Create Run ID").first().json.task_breaker_model,   temperature: 0.0,   max_tokens: 600,   think: false,    messages: [     {       role: "system",       content: `You are a Linux automation tool developer.  Create ONE small executable tool that performs the supplied task.  Choose either strict Bash or strict Python: - Prefer Bash for simple Linux/system operations. - Use Python only when it materially simplifies the task.  The tool must: - Perform only the requested task. - Be non-interactive. - Avoid destructive actions. - Never modify the target system unless explicitly required. - Check required commands before using them. - Handle errors. - Send useful results to stdout. - Send errors to stderr. - Exit 0 on success and non-zero on failure. - Be suitable for later execution inside a Docker sandbox.  Return ONLY valid JSON:  {   "language": "bash",   "filename": "tool.sh",   "purpose": "short description",   "code": "#!/bin/bash\\n...",   "expected_output": "short description" }  Rules: - language must be "bash" or "python". - filename must end in .sh or .py accordingly. - Generate exactly one tool. - Do not use markdown fences. - Do not explain the code outside the JSON.`     },     {       role: "user",       content: `MAJOR TASK:  ${$("Create Run ID").first().json.major_task}  SUBTASK:  ${JSON.stringify(   $("Parse Plan").first().json.plan.tasks[0],   null,   2 )}`     }   ] }) }}
